subject: Re: Reranker integration follow-up + evaluation questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@searchly.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@searchly.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — Reranker integration follow-up + next steps

Hi Elena / Tom,

Really appreciated the time today — great discussion on where Searchly is with relevance tuning and where a lightweight reranker could help tighten results for short-tail queries. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- What we heard from your side:
  - Primary signal gap: current ranking drifts on recency-sensitive queries and ambiguous intent queries (e.g., "invoice" vs "how to pay invoice").
  - Current infra: embeddings stored in Postgres (vector extension), existing retrieval pipeline written in Go, API gateway in GCP.
  - Success metric: +8–12% improvement in MRR for surfaced commercial queries (internal metric) or a +0.04 NDCG@10 on your evaluation set.

- How Redwood can help (integration overview):
  - Quick path: use Redwood embeddings + ranking API as a drop-in reranker (post-retrieval) to score top_k candidates.
  - SDKs: JavaScript/Go SDKs for server-side scoring; token/auth handled via API key or mTLS for Private deployments.
  - Tuning knobs: top_k (we recommend starting at 50 -> then tune to 10–20), combine score blending (retrieval_score * w1 + reranker_score * w2), and relevance thresholds for promotion.
  - Eval support: we can run an eval pass against your holdout set (we shared a tiny template).

Next steps I propose: 
1) You share a small sample eval set (CSV) with ~1k queries + graded relevance scores (or click labels) — I attached a lightweight template.
2) Connor (cc'ed) will confirm SDK/auth snippets and routing recommendations for your Go pipeline.
3) We run a 2-week pilot eval (Redwood runs reranker offline, returns metrics NDCG@k, MAP, precision@k) and reconvene to review results.

Please ping if that sequence looks right or if you prefer we start with a live integration demo instead. I'll follow up with Connor to outline the SDK snippet and auth options.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0182

Attachment: reranker_evals_template.csv (CSV template with columns: query_id, query_text, candidate_id, candidate_text, label)

From: Elena Park <elena@searchly.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@searchly.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — Reranker integration follow-up + next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A couple clarifying things from our engineering side before we hand over the eval set: 

- Auth: we prefer short-lived keys or mTLS for production. If you support short-lived keys with an exchange endpoint, that would be ideal.
- SDK: our retrieval pipeline is in Go and lives in a k8s cluster behind a service mesh (Istio). Would the JS/Go SDK work without extra egress work?
- Routing: for A/B, we want to split 10% of traffic to reranker and measure online delta. Does Redwood support per-route rollout and consistent hashing to keep sessions sticky?

Also attaching a quick architecture sketch and our sample eval (sanitized). The eval is ~1,200 queries with binary relevance labels.

Elena
VP Product
Searchly

Attachments: searchly_api_flow.drawio, searchly_eval_sample_1200.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@searchly.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@searchly.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — Reranker integration follow-up + next steps

Perfect — thanks for the files and the sketch. Looping in Dev and Connor to answer the implementation details. Quick answers up front: 

- Short-lived keys: supported. We provide a token-exchange endpoint (post-auth) that issues short-lived bearer tokens (30m–2h TTL) and rotateable client creds. For Private/VPC deployments we support mTLS and customer-controlled KMS.
- SDK + egress: the Go SDK can run as a sidecar or as a library in your service. Egress-wise, if you are on our hosted API you'll need outbound HTTPS to api.redwood.ai; for dedicated/private we can deploy within your VPC.
- Routing & rollouts: yes — Redwood Console supports route-level traffic splits (percent-based), consistent hashing for user/session stickiness, and can route by policy (region, model variant).

Connor / Dev — can you confirm a recommended top_k baseline (from our side) and the simplest scoring blend to try for an initial A/B? Also any specific Go snippet to paste back to Elena for the sidecar approach?

Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@searchly.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@searchly.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — Reranker integration follow-up + next steps

Hi all — quick technical answers & starter snippets below. Happy to hop on a 30-min tech call if helpful.

1) Top_k baseline: start with top_k=50 for offline eval (gives the reranker enough candidates), then tune down to top_k=10–20 for latency-sensitive online use. For initial A/B (10% traffic) I'd suggest scoring top_k=20 and setting blend = 0.4 * retrieval_score + 0.6 * reranker_score.

2) Metrics we recommend to report: NDCG@10, MRR, MAP, precision@K (K=1,5,10). For binary labels you can compute NDCG and precision easily; if you have graded labels we can compute gain-based metrics.

3) Go SDK snippet (sidecar call to Redwood scoring API):

// pseudo-Go snippet - call Redwood scoring endpoint with short-lived bearer token
client := http.Client{Timeout: 2 * time.Second}
reqBody := map[string]interface{}{
  "query": queryText,
  "candidates": candidatesJSON,
  "top_k": 20
}
req := newRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ranking/score", reqBody)
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer " + os.Getenv("REDWOOD_TOKEN"))
resp, _ := client.Do(req)
// parse reranker scores and blend with retrieval score client-side

4) Auth options: exchange endpoint example: POST /v1/tokens/exchange with client_cred -> returns ephemeral token (30m). We'll provide a Helm chart example if you want the sidecar deployed as a k8s Deployment.

5) Eval pipeline: we can run the eval on your CSV sample and return a short report. Please confirm you are comfortable with Redwood storing this sanitized sample temporarily (30 days) for the purposes of the pilot, or we can run the eval in your cloud account for Private/Dedicated customers.

Next steps from us: once you confirm storage preference and we get the CSV, we'll schedule the 2-week offline run and share the eval dashboard with NDCG/MRR/MAP breakdowns.

—Dev
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
